title: Canada’s Alphonso Davies set for a spell on the sidelines with hamstring injury
content:
Alphonso Davies is set for a spell on the sidelines with a hamstring injury suffered in the 6-1 win over Atalanta in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

The Canada international played just 25 minutes of Bayern’s last 16 first leg in Bergamo, having been introduced as a half-time substitute for Konrad Laimer, before sustaining the injury and being replaced by Tom Bischof.

The 25-year-old covered his face as he was forced off early, raising concerns about the injury and potentially his availability ahead of this summer’s World Cup.

In a statement on Wednesday afternoon, Bayern did not confirm a timeframe for his recovery, and the severity of the injury remains unclear.

However, the club does not appear to be seriously concerned, with head coach Vincent Kompany saying after Tuesday’s game: “It’s a muscular injury and we’ll have to get through some games without him.”

Davies has made 13 appearances across all competitions this season, having returned to action in December following nine months out with an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury.

He tore the ACL in his right knee while on international duty in March, with Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen accusing Canada Soccer of being “grossly negligent” in its handling of the injury.

The versatile full-back was also forced off early in the second half of Bayern’s win over Eintracht Frankfurt last month after sustaining a muscle fibre tear in his right hamstring, missing the subsequent league games against Borussia Dortmund and Monchengladbach.

The game against Atalanta was his first match back following that injury.

Canada is co-hosting the World Cup in June and July with the U.S. and Mexico. Jesse Marsch’s side are in Group B of the tournament alongside Qatar, Switzerland and a European play-off victor.

Analysis from The Athletic’s Canadian soccer writer Joshua Kloke

Davies has struggled with injuries throughout his career.

The ACL tear in March, while with the Canadian national team, caused him to miss most of 2025. Previously, Davies has sustained multiple muscle injuries as well as a bout with myocarditis that impacted his 2022 World Cup qualifying campaign.

When Davies has been fit, his form has bounced up and down since his all-world highs of 2023, when he was arguably the best left back in the world.

Davies’ game is built on speed on the flank. Any muscle injury could hurt how well he continues to perform both for Bayern and Canada.

If Davies is in strong form, he remains arguably Canada’s best player. His pace and crossing ability can fit well — offensively speaking — into Canada manager Jesse Marsch’s high-tempo system.

But because of injury, Davies has not yet made a consistent impact for Marsch as hoped. Davies wants to move into an advanced midfield role for the World Cup, which could offer the opportunity for a possible breakout tournament under Marsch.

Canada have potential cover at left-back: Richie Laryea was their best player in 2025 and should be a more than adequate in the position. Ali Ahmed or Liam Millar are both in contention for a starting left midfield role. Both have fans in Marsch.
